title: DO-loop iteration count is computed ONCE at entry — modifying the bound inside the loop is ignored
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE GROW_THEN_PROCESS(N, A, SUM)
C     The F77 standard says the trip count for DO is
C     MAX(0, (END - START + STEP) / STEP) computed BEFORE the
C     loop body. Re-assigning N inside the loop does not change
C     how many times the loop runs.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER N, I
      REAL    A(*), SUM
      SUM = 0.0
      DO I = 1, N
         SUM = SUM + A(I)
         IF (SUM .GT. 100.0) N = I
C        ^ Looks like an early exit -- it ISN'T. The loop still
C          runs to the ORIGINAL N.
      END DO
      END
notes: F77 DO loops do NOT honour modifications to the loop bound inside the body. Java/C# for-loops re-evaluate the condition each iteration — a literal port silently changes behaviour. The spec must surface this so the rewrite either uses a fixed trip count (preserve semantic) or an explicit break (intentional change).
